content_voiceover: This table addresses a high yield trap on boards, comorbid conditions that can independently cause microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, separate from classic TTP. Look at the pattern across every row, autoimmunity with ANA, ANCA, or antiphospholipid antibodies, HIV infection, hematopoietic stem cell transplant, solid organ transplant, malignant hypertension, pregnancy, and neoplastic disease. Each of these has its own mimic, vasculitis or catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome for autoimmunity, fungemia or viremia in HIV and transplant patients, antirejection or GVHD drugs, severe hypertension causing endothelial injury, preeclampsia and HELLP in pregnancy, and drug induced TMA or tumor embolism in malignancy. But notice that atypical HUS, AHUS, appears in almost every single row as a differential. That's the exam pearl, complement mediated TMA can be unmasked or triggered by any of these systemic stressors, so a normal ADAMTS13 level in a sick patient with MAHA and thrombocytopenia should prompt you to think about AHUS and these comorbid triggers, not just assume it's not TTP and stop there. Management often involves excluding infection, adjusting the offending drug, biopsy when needed, and empiric anti C5 therapy for suspected AHUS.
keypoints: AHUS is a recurring differential across nearly every comorbid TMA trigger
Autoimmune disease, HIV, HSCT, solid organ transplant, malignant HTN, pregnancy, malignancy all cause MAHA + thrombocytopenia independent of TTP
Exclude infection and offending drugs before empiric anti-C5 therapy
Normal ADAMTS13 does not rule out AHUS
keypoint_voiceover: When MAHA and thrombocytopenia occur with autoimmune disease, HIV, transplant, malignant hypertension, pregnancy, or cancer, don't stop at ruling out TTP, atypical HUS shows up as a differential in nearly every one of these settings. Work up infection, review culprit drugs, consider biopsy, and think about empiric anti-C5 therapy for suspected complement mediated TMA once other causes are excluded.
